name: trace.mermaid
title: Show graph as Mermaid
summary: The graph of one element as trace.graph gives it, written as a Mermaid flowchart: one node per element, one edge per link, without the evidence.
details: The same nodes and edges as `trace.graph` for the same input, as text. Each node shows the short ID with the identifier, the type, the title, the marks and the verification; each edge goes from the source to the target and is labelled with the name of its kind, and `outdated` when the link is outdated. The element has a thicker frame. The first line is a comment when the graph is cut by `limit` or incomplete. The CLI prints the text alone, so its output redirected to a file is a Mermaid diagram. A graph near the default `limit` of 500 nodes can be larger than Mermaid draws with its default settings (at most 500 edges and 50,000 characters of text); for a large graph ask with a smaller `maxDepth` or `limit`.

ref.description: The element whose graph is written: its UUID, short ID or identifier.

repository.description: The workspace name of the repository of the element ref names, as in element.get (ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#255).

maxDepth.description: The deepest level in each direction; 0: the element only. Omitted: 1 (the direct neighbours), unless `allLevels` is true.

allLevels.description: Go as far as the links go (the whole chain), within `limit`; not together with `maxDepth`. For the chain alone ask with `meanings: ["derivation"]`.

kinds.description: Keys of relation kinds or of properties of kind `relation` (such as `packages`) to follow. An unknown key is `input.invalid`. See `meanings` for the filter rule.

meanings.description: Relation kinds with these meanings are followed; `reference` stands for inline references. Without `kinds` and `meanings` every relation and reference is followed. Otherwise a link is followed when its key is in `kinds` or its meaning is in `meanings`; an empty list follows nothing.

view.description: Only the elements of the graph that this view holds: `core` or a variant ID; without it every element.

limit.description: The most nodes, the element included; the nearest levels first (`truncated` says when more exist).

mermaid.description: The Mermaid flowchart, bottom to top, LF line endings and a final newline. Labels are quoted, with `#`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `:` and `{` written as Mermaid entities in node labels and `&`, `<` and `>` in edge labels. In an edge label `"` becomes `'` and `%%{` becomes `%% {`; line breaks and other control characters become one space.

truncated.description: More elements are reachable than shown: `limit` stopped a walk or left out a node. The nodes kept are the nearest ones.

problems.description: Hints: `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no relation kind has the meaning `derivation` or no type the meaning `requirement`, so the verification status and degree of the nodes cannot be given in full (SR-013 AK3).
